name: Francis Fletcher, 'The Description of Elizabeth Iland', in John Conyers' 1677 copy (British Library, Sloane MS 61), reproduced as Plate IV in Zelia Nuttall, New Light on Drake (Hakluyt Society, Ser. II vol. 34, 1914)
licence: public domain (the drawing is 16th-17th century; the 1914 reproduction is out of copyright)
note: A drawing from the voyage: Fletcher was Drake's chaplain, and this is his picture of the island alone — a squarish island, slightly taller than wide, with a hatched shore, a freshwater pool and a stream, inside a dotted sea and a barber-pole border. Fletcher's originals are lost; Conyers' copy survives in Sloane MS 61, which the BL has not digitised, so Nuttall's plate is the best image. About 667 x 696 px on the leaf. Chosen by Etienne in October 2026 over Fletcher's own map of the three islands (Nuttall Plate III, where 'Insula Elizabetha' is ~60 x 70 px), Hondius' Drake broadside (c. 1595, ~20 x 25 px), the Drake-Mellon map (c. 1587, a ~26 x 16 px speck) and Delisle 1703, the story's plate, which draws only a stub of coast at its neatline. By the project's rule a drawing by the island's own discoverers beats any chart of it, as Yamada's sketch did for Nakanotorishima.
orientation_note: SOUTH-UP. The pool is labelled 'a Poole of freshwater in the south part of the Ile' and is drawn at the top; Fletcher's map on Plate III of the same manuscript is south-up too (the River Plate at the bottom, the Strait at the top). The trace is turned 180 degrees (--turn 180) to stand north-up. That is a reading of the drawing, not a liberty.
scale_note: None. Conyers writes under it 'This Iland Broader & deeper then the Originall', so even the drawing's size is not Fletcher's, and no scale is drawn. Size is set by hand (--height-km).
extraction_note: --mode ink, threshold 110 (110-130 is a plateau, 667 x 696 px): the coast is one continuous heavy line with short hatch strokes outside, so a flood from inside stops at it, and the pool and lettering are filled as holes. The stream runs from the pool to the north coast, which joins the pool to the sea side of the flood and leaves it cut out; the stream is painted out (--blank-box 1000,926,1032,1045), just inside the coastline, so the pool closes and fills. The atlas draws outer shores only, so the pool is land here. The edge sits on the inner side of the coast line, about 2% of the island's width.
